([[Orlando, Florida]]) | college = [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] (2018–2019) | draft_year = 2019 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 25 | draft_team = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | career_start = 2019 | years1 = {{nbay|2019|start}}–{{nbay|2022|end}} | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team2 = [[Phoenix Suns]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team3 = [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years4 = 2025–2026 | team4 = [[Chiba Jets]] | years5 = 2026-present | team5 = [[Saga Ballooners]] | highlights = *[[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] MVP ([[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]]) }} '''Nassir Shamai Little''' ({{IPAc-en|n|ə|ˈ|s|ɪər}} {{respell|nə|SEER}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born February 11, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Saga Ballooners]] of the Japanese [[B.League]]. Little finished his high school career as one of the top-ranked players in his class, having led [[Orlando Christian Prep]] to consecutive Florida state championships. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]] and was selected in the first round of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. ==Early life== Little played his freshman and sophomore seasons (2014–16) at [[Oakleaf High School]] then transferred to [[Orlando Christian Prep]], where he played for the rest of his high school career. In his junior and senior season (2016–18), he led Orlando Christian Prep to back-to-back Florida state titles.{{cite web|first=Randy|last=Lefko|title=Little drafted into NBA|url=https://www.claytodayonline.com/stories/little-goes-nba,17838|work=Clay Today|date=June 26, 2019|access-date=July 23, 2023}} Little stood out during the [[McDonald's All-American Game]] in [[2018 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2018]] as he posted 28 points and 5 rebounds, 1 assist and 1 steal, to lead the West past the East and claim the [[most valuable player]] (MVP) award. He also won MVP honors at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] after putting up 24 points in 25 minutes. Thus he joined [[LeBron James]] as only the second player to win MVP honors at both high school All-American games.{{cite web|title=Nassir Little Is Learning the Hard Way|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2811408-nassir-little-is-learning-the-hard-way|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=September 12, 2019}} Little was ranked the second-best high school prospect of 2018 by the recruiting service [[Rivals.com|Rivals]].{{cite news|first=Kyle|last=Boone|title=McDonald's All-American Game: North Carolina signee Nassir Little takes home MVP honors|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mcdonalds-all-american-game-north-carolina-signee-nassir-little-takes-home-mvp-honors/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 29, debut for the Tar Heels on November 6, 2018, recording 7 points, 3 assists, and 2 blocks during North Carolina's 78–67 victory over [[2018–19 Wofford Terriers men's basketball team|Wofford]].{{cite three assists. [...] He had two blocks.}} Little scored a career-high 23 points to go along with 6 rebounds and 3 assists as North Carolina defeated [[2018–19 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Virginia Tech]] 103–82.{{cite web|first=Maxwell|last=Underhill|title=UNC's Long-Awaited Nassir Little Awakening Should Scare Rest of ACC|url=https://www.12up.com/posts/6277628-unc-s-long-awaited-nassir-little-awakening-should-scare-rest-of-acc|website=12up.com|date=January 22, 2019|access-date=March 8, 2019|archive-date=February 5, 2019}} At the conclusion of his freshman season, Little announced his decision to forgo his collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2019 NBA draft]], where he was projected to be a first-round selection.{{cite news|first=Johnathan|last=Givony|title=UNC freshman Little declares for NBA Draft|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26417235|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 1, 2019|access-date=July 23, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2023)=== On June 20, 2019, the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] drafted Little with the 25th overall pick in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title= Nassir Little to Trail Blazers: Portland's Current Roster After 2019 NBA Draft|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2836234-nassir-little-to-trail-blazers-portlands-current-roster-after-2019-nba-draft|work=Bleacher Report|access-date=June 20, 2019}} On July 1, 2019, Little officially signed with the Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Nassir Little|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/story/2019/7/1/blazers-sign-nassir-little|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2019|access-date=July 2, 2019}} On February 1, 2021, Little scored a career-high 30 points to go along with 6 rebounds, 2 blocks, 1 assist and 1 steal.{{cite web|title=Bucks sizzle from 3-point range to blast Blazers 134-106|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401267476|website=ESPN.com|date=February 2, 2021|access-date=July 23, 2023|quote=Nassir Little led [...] with 30 points – 2 1/2 times [his] previous career high of 12.}} On January 27, 2022, Little suffered a left shoulder labral tear.{{cite news|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|authorlink=Adrian Wojnarowski|title=Portland Trail Blazers' Nassir Little likely done for season because of shoulder tear, sources say|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33160838|work=[[ESPN]]|date=January 27, 2022|access-date=January 27, 2022}} Four days later, the Trail Blazers announced he would undergo surgery and would miss the rest of the season.{{cite web|title=Nassir Little To Undergo Surgery On Left Shoulder|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/nassir-little-undergo-surgery-left-shoulder|website=NBA.com|date=January 31, 2022|access-date=July 23, 2023}} On May 10, Little underwent abdominal surgery on his left side.{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Fentress|title=Portland Trail Blazers' Nassir Little undergoes core muscle surgery|url=https://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/2022/05/portland-trail-blazers-nassir-little-undergoes-core-muscle-surgery.html|website=OregonLive.com|date=May 10, 2022|access-date=July 23, 2023}} On October 17, 2022, it was announced Little agreed on a four-year, $28 million contract extension with the Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Nassir Little to Multi-Year Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-nassir-little-to-multi-year-contract-extension|website=NBA.com|date=October 17, 2022|access-date=July 23, 2023}} In mid-April 2023, Little underwent abdominal surgery on his right side.{{cite web|first=Casey|last=Holdahl|title=Nassir Little Undergoes Abdominal Surgery|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/nassir-little-undergoes-abdominal-surgery|website=NBA.com|date=April 13, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2023}} ===Phoenix Suns (2023–2024)=== On September 27, 2023, Little, alongside [[Grayson Allen]], [[Jusuf Nurkić]], and [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]] was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] as part of a three-team trade that sent [[Damian Lillard]] to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and [[Jrue Holiday]], [[Toumani Camara]], [[Deandre Ayton]], and a 2029 first-round draft pick to the Portland Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=SUNS ACQUIRE NURKIĆ, ALLEN, LITTLE, JOHNSON|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-acquire-nurkic-allen-little-johnson|website=NBA.com|date=September 27, 2023|access-date=September 27, 2023}} On August 27, 2024, Little was waived by the Suns.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Amico|title=Suns Officially Waive Two Players|url=https://hoopswire.com/suns-nba-news-transactions-ej-liddell-nassir-little/|website=HoopsWire.com|date=August 27, 2024|access-date=August 27, 2024}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2024–2025)=== On September 24, 2024, Little signed with the [[Miami Heat]],{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN NASSIR LITTLE|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-nassir-little|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}} but was waived on October 19.{{cite web|title=HEAT WAIVE LITTLE, PULLIN, STEVENS AND WASHINGTON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-waive-little-pullin-stevens-and-washington|website=NBA.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web|title=Skyforce Announces Training Camp Roster Ahead of 2024-25 Season|url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-training-camp-roster-ahead-of-2024-25-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 31, 2024}} In 32 appearances with the Skyforce, Little averaged 16.7 points and 6.3 rebounds per game. ===Chiba Jets (2025–present)=== On July 16, 2025, Little signed with the [[Chiba Jets]] of the Japanese [[B.League]].{{cite web|title= ナシール・リトル選手　B.LEAGUE2025-26シーズン選手契約基本合意（新規）のお知らせ |url= https://chibajets.jp/news/detail/id=23599 |website=chibajets.jp|date=July 16, 2025|access-date=July 19,
